'are small beside it' is deleted. In its place, in the BRIEF Rate limits bullet and in DISCOVERY U-16, is per-app arithmetic labelled as arithmetic, not a GitHub figure. An access token lasts 8 hours (E-02 line 34), so a MoonAliza running all day refreshes about 3 times a day. Across all users that is about active users x 3 / 24 refreshes an hour, which reaches 2,000 at about 16,000 users active across a day. This matters only if refreshes count toward the limit and the limit counts per app; GitHub states neither. It is kept as part of U-16's product risk.

Decision Refresh now refreshes, single-flight, when fewer than 5 minutes (300 s) remain. Expiry is the local time the token response was received plus expires_in. This is labelled a design choice: GitHub gives the 8-hour lifetime (E-01 line 174, E-02 line 34) but no margin. The margin matches the spec's refreshMarginMs. 'An expired token never reaches GitHub' became 'an expired token is not sent knowingly; a token that expires in flight, or after a local clock change, can still reach GitHub (Known unknowns)', and the Decision says how a 401 or a 404 is then handled. findings.problem: The fresh-token guard (DC-2) can loop, refreshing on every read with no hold and never clearing the account. When the guard runs out (three 401s on a token under 5 s old), it throws GITHUB_RENEWAL_UNAVAILABLE and sets no hold. On the next read more than 5 s later, the same token is no longer 'fresh', so the 401 rule refreshes again instead of clearing. That refresh succeeds and resets `hold` and `failures`, and its new token meets the guard again. Two cases trigger it: (a) GitHub persistently rejects tokens that a refresh just issued; (b) GitHub's propagation delay is longer than about 3 s and the model rereads 5-8 s apart. In case (b) every reread rotates the pair before it propagates. Each read then costs one refresh on the shared per-app endpoint (U-16), the dialog shows no `renewalHeld`, and the account never reaches 'sign in again'. This is the same class of defect as DC-1. In production the C-6 clear inside a call can no longer happen: the retry always follows the refresh within 5 s.
findings.evidence: Spec 6.4 l.683-692: the fresh branch throws RENEWAL_UNAVAILABLE when `budget.fresh === 2` and calls no `failed()`. For a token at least 5 s old with an unspent budget, it reaches `budget.refreshed = true ... waitRefresh`. 6.5 l.753: a successful refresh sets `hold = null; failures = 0`. Three statements become false: 6.5 l.761 ('at most once per expiry window, plus once per hold period while failing. Never once per request'); known limit 15, l.1094 ('A token GitHub really rejected meets the 401 rule on the next read after those 5 s', where in fact the rule refreshes); DECISIONS DR-4 trade-offs l.190 ('keeps the account for up to 5 s longer'). Refresh test 10 (l.1227) tests C-6 only by moving the injected clock past `freshTokenMs`, a state real timing never reaches.
findings.fix: When the guard runs out, call `failed()`, so the doubling hold blocks further refreshes. Count consecutive guard exhaustions toward `maxSameRefreshError`, and clear the account as `sign-in-ended` after 3. Also, do not refresh on a 401 for a token a refresh produced less than `transientHoldMs` ago; fail with the hold's reason instead. Correct the wording in 6.5 l.761, known limit 15 and DR-4 (l.190). Add two tests. (1) The fake accepts every refresh but answers 401 to every resource request; reads run 6 s apart for 5 minutes. Expect a bounded number of refresh requests (at most 3), the account ending `sign-in-ended`, and `renewalHeld` true in between. (2) The fake answers 401 until 8 s after a token is issued, and reads run 6 s apart. Expect recovery after exactly one refresh.

findings.problem: DC-1 is only partly fixed. Only answers that carry an `error` code count toward the three-in-a-row clear. An `unusable` refresh answer (a 3xx, a 4xx without `error` such as a JSON `message` body or an HTML page, or a 2xx without `access_token`) calls `failed()` and resets `sameError`. A dead account is therefore held, with doubling holds, until the refresh token expires up to six months later, and it is never cleared. If DO-1 fails with such an answer, the user stays 'Signed in as <login>' and every read fails as renewal-unavailable. UD-6's 'Why' implies every failing second refresh ends in 'sign in again'.
findings.evidence: Spec 5.3 rows 2 and 8 (l.560, l.566): such answers are `unusable`. 6.5 l.741: `if r is not error -> sameError = null`. l.748: `unusable, transient -> failed()`. USER-DECISIONS UD-6 'Why' l.79 and DO-1 l.100 promise the clear only 'for any other code'. No test feeds a non-`error` 4xx refresh answer three times.
findings.fix: Treat consecutive identical `unusable` answers like unknown codes: key `sameError` by `status:<n>` and clear after `maxSameRefreshError`. Keep hold-only behaviour for `transient` (network, timeout, 5xx). If clearing is judged too aggressive behind a proxy, state instead in DO-1 and UD-6 that such an answer holds rather than clears, and have DO-1 record it. Add refresh test 4b: a 401 with a JSON `message` body three times either clears the account after at most 3 requests, or is documented as held.

findings.problem: `rollback()` (DC-11) can restore a stale file. It runs as a separate `serialized(file)` call after `replace` throws, so any writer already queued on the lock runs between the two. A refresh of the old account A that waited while the sign-in held the lock is admitted: `generation` is unchanged and `live` is still A. That refresh writes A' to the file, commits it, sets `live = A'`, then retires and removes A and S. `rollback` then writes the step-4 snapshot back, so the file names A, whose refs are now removed, and its revision goes backwards. Until the next rotation, `live` is A' but the file names dead refs. If MoonAliza restarts first, the user is signed out and A' is left as orphan committed entries that the reconcile never deletes.
findings.evidence: `src/models/artifact-files.ts:59-63`: `serialized` is a FIFO promise chain per key, so queued tasks run before `rollback`'s task. Spec 4.3 l.474: rollback 'writes the file back to the account and retiredRefs kept at step 4 (revision + 2)' with no check that the file is unchanged. 6.3 l.654: rollback is called only after the throw. 6.5 l.750: the refresh admit is `generation === g0 && live?.accessRef === from.accessRef`, and both still hold because a failed sign-in does neither `generation++` nor set `live`. `src/main/vault.ts:106-121`: the reconcile never deletes committed entries.
findings.fix: Do the rollback inside `replace` while it still holds the lock: a sign-in passes an option such as `onCommitFailure: 'rollback'`, and `replace` returns a distinct result. Alternatively, have `rollback` compare the file's revision with the one step 4 wrote. If the file has moved on, write nothing and only tombstone and remove the new refs the current file does not name. Add a store test: the commit fails for a sign-in while a refresh `replace` is queued behind it. After rollback, the file and `live` agree, and reopening plus reconciling gives the refreshed account with no orphan entries.

findings.problem: During a hold, `usable()` refuses an access token that is still valid. In the last 300 s before expiry, any active hold, including the new doubling hold, makes reads fail as GITHUB_RENEWAL_UNAVAILABLE or GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT, although the token still works and L-5 allows sending it when no refresh is possible. A transient refresh failure at T-299 s blocks every read for the whole hold, even though GitHub would accept them.
findings.evidence: Spec `usable()` step 4, l.699-701: 'if a hold is active, throw hold.reason and send nothing (L-13)'. Step 5, l.702, already sends a still-valid token when the refresh token has expired. L-5, l.121: 'within the 300 s margin, when a refresh is possible'. L-13, l.149, restricts refresh requests, not reads. REQUIREMENTS F-6, l.88: 'Calls during a hold fail at once'.
findings.fix: In step 4, when a hold is active, fall through to step 5: send the token while `accessExpiresAt > t`, and throw `hold.reason` only once it has expired. Reword F-6 to 'Calls that need a refresh during a hold fail at once'. Add a test: with a hold active and the token 200 s from expiry, the read is sent with that token and no refresh request is made.

findings.problem: Nothing tests or injects the link between `REQUEST_OFFLINE_ACCESS` and the service (DC-3). The constants test pins the value and the oauth test pins `requestDeviceCode(..., offlineAccess)`. A service that passes a literal `true` would pass both, so UD-6's fallback (flip the constant) would silently keep sending `scope=offline_access`. REQUIREMENTS T-3 claims a device-flow test 'step 1 without scope when REQUEST_OFFLINE_ACCESS is false', but the spec's device tests 1-16 do not list it, and `GitHubSignInDeps.config` offers no way to set it. Mocking the module is hazardous under `isolate: false`.
findings.evidence: Spec 3.1, l.181; 3.7, l.349 (`config?: { clientId; installUrl }` only); 6.1 step 4, l.612; device tests l.1178-1197; guard table, l.1410 ('the constants test; the oauth request shapes'). REQUIREMENTS T-3, l.130. `vitest.config.ts:12`: `isolate: false`.
findings.fix: Add `offlineAccess?: boolean` to `GitHubSignInDeps.config`, defaulting to `REQUEST_OFFLINE_ACCESS`; it is a test seam, not a setting. Add device test 2b with two cases. With `offlineAccess: false`, the step-1 body keys are exactly `{client_id}`. With default construction, they are `{client_id, scope}`, so the default is proved to read the constant. List both cases in the guard table.

findings.problem: The spec contradicts itself on what `send()` may throw. 3.4 and BREAKDOWN U5 say it throws only `CREDENTIAL_ERRORS` (or rejects when the signal aborts). 6.4 `withAccess` step 5 lets a fetch failure and ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE pass through, and `renew` leaves local vault failures inside `withRefresh` unclassified: ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE, a missing `.bin` file, a failed decrypt. A builder who enforces 3.4 would map a network error on a signed-in read to GITHUB_RENEWAL_UNAVAILABLE. That text tells the model to ask the user to sign in again, where today's GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE says nothing of the kind. A builder who follows 6.4 breaks a typed contract and any test written from it.
findings.evidence: Spec 3.4, l.268: 'Throws only a member of CREDENTIAL_ERRORS, or rejects when signal aborts.' BREAKDOWN U5 row, l.126: 'Throws only CREDENTIAL_ERRORS from send()'. Spec 6.4 `withAccess` step 5, l.722: 'Other errors pass through: a fetch failure, or ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE'. 6.5 l.739-740 classifies only DENIED from `withRefresh`. `src/main/vault.ts:158-161`: `withSecret` can throw ENOENT, ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE or a decrypt error. `src/main/github.ts:80-81`: non-GITHUB_ errors become GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE.
findings.fix: Change 3.4 and the U5 row to: 'send() originates only CREDENTIAL_ERRORS; it rethrows the request's own rejection and ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE unchanged (the reader maps them to GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE).' In `renew`, classify local vault failures as `failed()`: nothing was sent, but it holds. Add a test: when the refresh token's decrypt throws, the read gets GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE (or the chosen reason), the token endpoint gets zero requests, and a second read within the hold makes no decrypt attempt.

findings.problem: The design assumes a GitHub behaviour that the corpus does not state and no day-one check covers: an access token killed by a refresh gets 401. The 401 rule's 'rotated meanwhile, retry with the current token' path (F-8) depends on it. E-02 says only that the old token 'will no longer work'. The corpus gives 401 for revoked tokens and calls a 404 plausible for expired ones. If a rotation-killed token gets 404 on a private repository, a read in flight during a rotation reports GITHUB_NOT_FOUND_SIGNED_IN ('may not exist ... not installed') instead of retrying.
findings.evidence: E-02 capture l.36: 'Once you use a refresh token, that refresh token and the old user access token will no longer work.' E-01 l.44: a revoked token gets '401 Bad Credentials'. DISCOVERY U-5: for an expired token, '404 is plausible by analogy, not stated'. Spec 6.4 l.688 (the rotated path acts on a 401 only); 7.2 step 2 (a 404 becomes NOT_FOUND_SIGNED_IN). DO-5 (USER-DECISIONS l.104) covers expired tokens only.
findings.fix: Extend DO-1, or DO-5: after the first refresh, send `GET /user` and a private read with the access token that the refresh just retired, and record the statuses. List it in spec 'Day one' and REQUIREMENTS A-4. Until it is checked, say in known limit 5 that a read in flight across a rotation may show the signed-in 404 text.

findings.problem: `GET /user` carries the access token, but neither its request options nor a test pin `redirect: 'manual'` and `credentials: 'omit'` for it. 5.1 states those options for 'every OAuth request', and the login request is not an OAuth request. `fetchLogin`'s contract names only the 64 KiB bound, and its tests check only the `login` filter and a 401. S-4 ('No redirect is followed with a credential') therefore has no test for this request, and a builder may use fetch's default `redirect: 'follow'`.
findings.evidence: Spec 5.1, l.522-534 ('Every OAuth request uses: redirect: manual, ...', then a table that includes Login); 3.5, l.304 (the `fetchLogin` comment: '64 KiB; keeps only login; any failure is null'); oauth tests, l.1159 (`fetchLogin`: login only, 401 gives null); guard table, l.1394 ('oauth shape pin; read twin'). REQUIREMENTS S-4, l.118.
findings.fix: State that `fetchLogin` uses `redirect: 'manual'`, `credentials: 'omit'`, `cache: 'no-store'` and the 20 s signal. Add oauth tests: the login init's exact keys; a 302 gives `null` after exactly one fetch, and the Location host receives nothing. Add the row to the guard table.

findings.problem: Refresh test 6 cannot prove the `transientHoldMs` floor on a rate-limit hold, although the guard table says it does. With the 30 s floor removed, `rateLimitWait`'s 1 s floor still holds the account. The two reads run at the same injected time, so only one refresh is sent either way, and the test stays green with its guard removed.
findings.evidence: Spec refresh test 6, l.1218 ('A 429 with retry-after: 0, followed by two reads, sends one refresh request in total'); 5.4, l.580 (the 1 s clamp); 6.5, l.742 (`max(w, transientHoldMs)`); guard table, l.1401 ('the refresh hold's transientHoldMs floor | ... refresh 6').
findings.fix: In refresh test 6, advance the injected clock 2 s after the 429. A read there must send no refresh (proving the 30 s floor) and `renewalHeld` must be true. At 31 s, one more refresh follows. Record the removal run for each floor separately.

findings.problem: A refresh that overlaps the login read (F5) loses the login for good. `renew` builds the new account with `from.login`, a snapshot taken before F5's `setLogin`, and `setLogin` applies only while `live.accessRef` is still the sign-in's ref. Whichever completes first, the login ends up null: the refresh overwrites it with `from.login = null`, or `setLogin` finds the rotated ref and does nothing. L-2 allows no second `GET /user` until another sign-in. The trigger needs a 401 at 5-20 s on the just-issued token, or a token issued with under 300 s left. It is rare, but its cause is in the contract.
findings.evidence: Spec 6.5, l.750: `store.replace(tokens, receivedAt, from.login, ...)`. 3.6, l.326: `setLogin` acts 'only while live.accessRef === accessRef'. 6.3 step 3, l.664-668. L-2, l.111-117.
findings.fix: For a refresh, have `replace` copy `live.login`, read under the lock, instead of the caller's snapshot. Let `setLogin` apply while the live account descends from the same sign-in, for example by an in-memory sign-in id carried across refreshes. Add a test: a refresh commits during a slow F5, and the login is set after both complete.

findings.problem: Two passages promise more than the revised design does. (1) REQUIREMENTS F-8 still says the account is cleared 'only when the refresh returns bad_refresh_token or the retried call still gets 401'. Since DC-1 and DC-2 that is wrong in both directions: other codes, three identical unknown codes and a malformed 2xx also clear the account, and a retry 401 on a token under 5 s old does not. (2) `ClearResult 'removed'` counts a durable tombstone persist alone. The dialog then says 'MoonAliza deleted its copy of your GitHub sign-in from this computer', yet step 3's `remove` may have failed, for example because a Windows file lock stopped the unlink, leaving the encrypted `.bin` files until the next start's reconcile.
findings.evidence: REQUIREMENTS F-8, l.90 (the 'only when' sentence), against F-7 (l.89) and spec L-12 (l.140-148). Spec 3.6, l.315-316 ('removed: the clear reached disk (a tombstone persist or the file write)'); 4.3, l.485; 6.7, l.790; 8.2, l.949. `src/main/vault.ts:172-180`: `remove` unlinks and can fail independently.
findings.fix: (1) Reword F-8 to defer to L-12: 'The account is cleared only in the L-12 cases; for the 401 rule, a retry that still gets 401 on a token at least 5 s old.' (2) Return 'removed' only when step 3's removals succeeded. Otherwise return a third value, such as 'tombstoned', and change the text to say MoonAliza stopped using its copy and deletes it when it next starts. Alternatively, reword the first sentence for all cases. Add the store test: tombstone persist succeeds, `remove` fails, and the expected result and text follow.
